claims.text: Adaptive bias force or metadynamics can substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for high-entropy systems.
Adaptive bias force or metadynamics improves the convergence of free-energy calculations.
The proposed technique is applicable to solid and fluid states near phase transitions.
The proposed technique can preserve faithful free energies for both solid and fluid states.
Enhanced sampling can retain vibrational-entropy contributions in free-energy calculations.
Enhanced sampling can retain anharmonic contributions in free-energy calculations.
Enhanced sampling can retain electron–vibration coupling in free-energy calculations.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost relative to TOR-TILD for high-entropy systems.
The proposed method will improve fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will improve fidelity relative to TOR-TILD.
The proposed compositional scope includes elemental, binary, and multicomponent systems.
The proposed temperature scope is near phase transitions.
The effectiveness of the advanced-sampling method may depend on the specific system and phase transition.
Failure to reproduce reference free energies and derived observables within 1–2% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improved fidelity relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD, but the benchmark treats those workflows as references and tests only agreement with them. Agreement within 1–2% cannot establish fidelity superior to the reference methods.
